title: Build Power BI reports with Direct Lake tables

claims.text: A semantic model containing Direct Lake tables is consumed exactly like any other Power BI semantic model: it supports reports, explorations, and DAX queries with no special client handling.

When a report visual requests data from a Direct Lake table, the semantic model reads the Delta table in OneLake directly and may retain recently accessed data in an in-memory cache to serve subsequent queries efficiently.

A Direct Lake on SQL table can fall back to DirectQuery through the SQL analytics endpoint when Direct Lake mode cannot be used, and this fallback is governed by the model's Direct Lake behavior property.

Reports built on a published semantic model use a live connection, so the report can be authored and edited without changing the model itself; at least Build permission on the model is required to live-connect.

Live-connecting to a published semantic model is distinct from live-editing that model in Power BI Desktop, and also distinct from authoring a local model with Import or DirectQuery tables bundled with the report.
Report-level measures can be defined inside a live-connected report in Power BI Desktop, which adds a calculation for that report without writing any measure into the shared semantic model.

Reports against a semantic model can be created from many entry points: Power BI Desktop via the OneLake catalog, the workspace context menu, the model details page, or web modeling's create-new-report option.

Beyond interactive reports, a semantic model also serves paginated reports, data explorations, ad-hoc DAX queries (including DAX query view), and refreshable Excel pivot or flat tables through the Analyze in Excel integration.
